reason: T1 human sign-off — feature story for call-dialer-primary-secondary. The requirement set is complete and locked: 19 functional requirements (FR-CDP-001..019) — Settings Primary + Fallback dialer pickers for the four channels (faceTime / phone / messenger / whatsApp) persisted through the AppCoordinator UserDefaults seam (secondaryCallApp, default .phone); the per-channel feasibility contract (Messenger ⇔ handle on file — never gated on the app being installed; WhatsApp ⇔ canOpenURL probed through an injected closure, local-only; FaceTime and phone always feasible); the pure-static chain resolver (preferred → secondary → phone) with equal-pick dedupe, at-most-once attempts, fellBackFrom carried in attempt order for announcements, and the never-dead-ends guarantee; explicit per-contact/family picks winning as the chain's preferred input (an infeasible explicit pick moves to the settings fallback, not the settings primary); every call path routed (address-book rows, family-contact buttons, missed-call dial-back, and voice-initiated calls via MethodResolver's global-default step, mapped CallApp→CallMethod by call type); fallback resolved BEFORE the existing spoken confirmation, which names the actually-routed channel ("Messenger isn't available — call Syanu via WhatsApp, okay?") with the override protocol (होइन, फोन नै गर) and near-miss disclosure preserved unchanged; launch-fail fallback hops down the chain announced through the existing spoken-outcome lane (never silent); automatic routing with a spoken announcement — no ask-before-fallback step; ne/en localization for all new strings; preserved behaviours (emergency-contact semantics untouched, no new dialogue flow, no silent failures, no CallRouter service, no per-contact primary/secondary storage); and the DV-1..7 device-validation completion gate. 10 non-functional requirements (NFR-CDP-001..010: exhaustive never-dead-end configuration matrix; 0 new network egress — probes local-only; log safety for numbers/handles incl. check-release-log-safety.sh coverage of the new paths; ≤ 100 ms added resolution latency; persistence round-trip; picker accessibility; ne/en localization parity; deterministic scoped-suite gate; no-regression baselines for the just-shipped voice pipeline, PRs #161–#168; compliance/release gates). 83 Gherkin acceptance scenarios. Open decisions: none — the design was owner-approved and frozen 2026-10-12 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-call-dialer-primary-secondary-design.md, committed on the feature branch) and the feature constitution records none. The owner is asked to approve the requirement elaboration as written before design work begins.
